% note: In the reading columns, ``\ensuremath{>}~margin'' stands for ``by more than the margin'': ``worse by \ensuremath{>}~margin'' is worse by more than the margin, as the other tables of this supplement write it.
% note: Holm's correction runs within each study only; the two studies are never pooled. At Study~1's 10-point margin (its only confirmatory margin; a secondary 5-point view is in ⟦TAB-03⟧) only Test~5 was shown no worse (Holm-adjusted), and at Study~1b's primary 5-point margin only B2. Tests~1--4, B1 and B3 carry the pre-registered decision rule's reading of the unadjusted 95\% interval, which is never a Holm-adjusted result.
% note: At Study~1b's pre-registered secondary 10-point margin, quoted only as the secondary, B1, B2 and B3 were each shown no worse than Opus-medium by more than the margin (Holm-adjusted; B1: $p$~=~0.00027, below its Holm threshold of 0.0125; B2: $p$~\ensuremath{\leq}~0.00011, below its Holm threshold of 0.00833; B3: $p$~\ensuremath{\leq}~0.00108, below its Holm threshold of 0.025).
% note: \ensuremath{\leq}~marks a $p$ at the smallest value the bootstrap can return (no resample reached the margin).
% note: Under the original pre-registered marking rule, which Deviation~2 kept as a sensitivity check (fixed in Lock~3, before any main-run data; not a pre-registered secondary view), Sonnet-medium's chain score is 55.00\% instead of 80.00\% (format compliance 65.00\% instead of 97.50\%). Test~3 would read inconclusive ($d$~=~+0.30 points, 95\% interval \mbox{[\ensuremath{-}13.58, 14.95]}) instead of worse by more than the margin. Test~5's reading is unchanged ($d$~=~+41.25 points, 95\% interval \mbox{[28.75, 52.50]}).
% note: Sonnet ran at medium effort, one level below its default (high), in Tests~3 and 5.
% note: Study~1's tests were pre-registered at 24 steps and run at 6 steps (Deviation~1).
% note: B2's accuracy is the expected accuracy of a vote of $k$~=~6 Haiku-max samples, computed from the 10 designed samples per puzzle and shape (no vote of that size was run separately); $k$ was measured from the two settings' mean list costs per sample. Per shape, the vote costs \$0.0736 per answer on chains against Opus-medium's \$0.0674, and \$0.0605 on pieces against \$0.0825 (list price).
% note: $d$ (points): the challenger (named first) minus the comparator, in accuracy points, paired over puzzles (in Study~1b both shapes of a puzzle are pooled); a positive $d$ means the challenger scored higher. Shapes: 1\ensuremath{\times}6 is the chain form of a puzzle and 6\ensuremath{\times}1 the pieces form. $k$ (Tests~1--3): the size of the cost-matched Haiku-medium vote, the most samples whose combined mean cost fits within the comparator's mean cost per puzzle; the $k$ computation prices each call at the Batch rate, exactly half the list price, so $k$ is the same at list prices (B2's $k$ is in the note above). Test~1's $k$ is capped at 40, the number of samples drawn per puzzle and shape, from the cost-matched 44.
% note: $k$, spend share and cost ratio (none is tested; $k$ is defined in the notes above). Each cell of the spend share or cost ratio column names its quantity; spend shares and the cost ratios of Test~4, B1 and B3 print to three decimals and Test~5's cost ratio to two, as ⟦TAB-05⟧ prints it. Spend share: Tests~1--3, the vote's realised spend over the comparator's at list price (pre-specified descriptive); B2, the vote's list cost per answer over Opus-medium's, as reported beside the test (pre-specified descriptive). Cost ratio: Test~4, step voting's mean list cost per puzzle over Opus-medium's, computed for this table from the two reported means (post hoc arithmetic on pre-specified means); Test~5, Opus-low's list cost per answer over Sonnet-medium's with its 95\% interval, labelled exploratory, no test (intervals two-sided, unadjusted); B1 and B3, the challenger's list cost per answer over Opus-medium's, as reported beside each test (pre-specified descriptive). The file's own words for one Haiku-max sample's cost are, for B1, ``about 1/6 of the cost per answer ($k$ measured)'' and, for B3, ``about 1/10 of the cost per answer ($k$ measured)''.
% note: Error-rate ratio (pre-specified descriptive, reported beside the test; not part of any test's reading): the challenger's errors over the comparator's. An unbounded upper end comes from bootstrap draws in which the comparator made no errors.
% note: Test~1's error-rate ratio is undefined: the comparator made no errors, so its error rate is at most 4.51\%, the upper end of the exact 95\% interval.
